description: Accounting concepts retrieved by the knowledge base search and attached to review issues as explanations.

entries.title: Debit and credit
entries.text: Every transaction has equal debit and credit effects. Assets and expenses increase with a debit; liabilities, income and capital increase with a credit. Total debits must equal total credits.

entries.title: Golden rules of accounting (Indian practice)
entries.text: Personal accounts: debit the receiver, credit the giver. Real accounts: debit what comes in, credit what goes out. Nominal accounts: debit expenses and losses, credit incomes and gains.

entries.title: Member receipts in a housing society
entries.text: A member payment settles the member's dues: bank account is debited and the member's account (receivable for the bill head, e.g. maintenance) is credited. The receipt must identify the flat, amount, date, mode and a bank/cheque reference so it can be matched to the bank statement.

entries.title: Bill heads
entries.text: Bill heads (maintenance, sinking fund, water charges, parking, etc.) are society-specific income heads. The code used for each head comes from the society's configuration (Mapping_Master), not from the document.

entries.title: Vendor bills
entries.text: A vendor bill debits the expense (or asset) head for the taxable value, debits GST input accounts when credit is claimed, credits TDS payable for tax deducted, and credits the vendor for the net payable.

entries.title: Petty cash register
entries.text: Petty cash is replenished by withdrawals from the bank (cash received) and spent on small expenses, each supported by a voucher. Closing balance = opening balance + cash received - cash paid. Each payment row should have a date, voucher number, particulars and amount.

entries.title: Imprest system
entries.text: Under an imprest system the petty cashier holds a fixed float that is topped up by the amount spent. The float amount is a society policy.

entries.title: Cash book
entries.text: A cash book records receipts on the debit side and payments on the credit side; the balance carried down must equal the physical cash.

entries.title: Bank reconciliation
entries.text: Receipts recorded from member acknowledgements must match credits in the bank statement by date, amount and UTR/cheque number.

entries.title: Duplicate entries
entries.text: The same voucher number, or the same date, amount and particulars recorded twice, indicates a possible duplicate posting and must be reviewed before posting.

entries.title: Handwritten amounts
entries.text: Handwritten Indian registers end amounts with '/-' (e.g. 900/-). OCR often reads the '/' as the digit 1, producing 9001. Ambiguous readings must be resolved against column totals or confirmed by a reviewer, never guessed.

entries.title: Indian digit grouping
entries.text: Indian grouping writes the last three digits together and earlier digits in pairs: 1,08,300 = 108300. Western grouping 108,300 is also common on printed documents.

entries.title: Register period
entries.text: Entries in a monthly register should be dated within that month and generally in chronological order.
